findings.location: sections 2-3, especially lines 55 and 70-85; plan.md AD-7/Persistence and Migration; tasks.md T040
findings.evidence: The corrected model makes PreparedScanManifestId, FileCodeUnitIdentityFingerprint, and PairSelectionOrdinal nullable on CodeUnit so historical rows remain valid, but then declares an alternate principal key containing those fields for the selected-audit composite FK. In EF Core, alternate-key properties are key properties and become required; a filtered unique index cannot substitute as an FK principal key. The current CodeUnit mapping already uses EF alternate keys, so implementing the planned key either makes the new columns non-null and breaks historical CodeUnit rows, or cannot create the claimed EF/PostgreSQL relationship. T040 repeats the contradictory nullable-shape plus filtered-FK requirement without choosing a feasible persistence seam.
findings.correction_outcome: Regenerate the plan set with an EF Core/PostgreSQL-feasible same-manifest association that preserves historical nullable CodeUnit rows—for example, a prepared-only principal/entry table with non-null association columns, or another explicitly mapped relational shape whose referenced key is a valid non-null principal constraint. Retain all audit canonical preimage columns and independent replay reconstruction. Update the data model, canonical/prepared contracts, migration ownership, and PostgreSQL lifecycle/atomicity tasks to prove both schema feasibility and legacy compatibility.
